name: The Low Market
descriptionSeed: The Low Market — the honest end of the Descent's trade: bargains with the terms written down. Not far enough down to be the Maw, not near enough the Crossing to be respectable. Everything is for sale and the price is on it.
encounterFlavor: traders, apprentices and people from three domains who have learned to share a street
axisVectorNote: Derived from authored spectrum against world_node_atlas.axisOrder (SNG-180). ⚠️ Every component is |0.45| or less by construction: a foothill is not extreme on any axis, which is what distinguishes it from its pole capital.

_worldPosWas_20261004.why: SNG-676: placed at half its pole's longitude (averaged with the Crossing's 0, which the pole does not have); moved onto the_maw's bearing (Erik 2026-10-04).

worldPosNote: SNG-676 (Erik 2026-10-04): ON ITS POLE'S BEARING, between the Crossing and its pole. The Crossing is the pole and has no longitude, so the line from it to anywhere runs along that place's own meridian; the first placement averaged with the Crossing's stored 0 and halved every bearing. Distance is the nearest dry solid land to the old one.
appearance: An orderly market of roofed stalls along a descending stone gallery, each with a written board hung above it. Lamps at fixed intervals. Goods stacked in the open, tallies and ledgers on the counters.
_axisRenamed_20260919: ⛔ SNG-632 — `order_chaos` WAS A REVERSED DUPLICATE OF `chaos_order`. Found in Erik's own dev report from this morning: seven spectrum pushes dropped, one of them on `order_chaos`, and I assumed the GM had constructed the name backwards. ⚠️ IT HAD NOT. The name is in the AUTHORED WORLD — five locations and a craft — and the GM read it off the corpus correctly. ⛑ `chaos_order` is canonical (67 locations, and the only one the GM prompt offers); `order_chaos` had ZERO readers in the engine, so every value written under it was inert. ⛔ THE SIGN IS PRESERVED, NOT FLIPPED: `poleIntensity` derives `order` from it directly, so Plainstead's `order_chaos: 0.25` already meant `order: 0.25` — a town of square stone on a swept grid, mildly ordered. The rename keeps the meaning and gives it a reader.
